wiki_article:
**EA-OPSEM-IDP-01** is the indexed document package for *Operative Semiotics*, deposited 2026-08-16 by Rebekah Cranes for the Institute for Diagrammatic Poetics, and the first deposit for the operativesemiotics.org surface.

The package exists because the work is whole in the archive and not whole at its own address. Sixteen deposits carry components of *Operative Semiotics*, but the monograph record (#1079) holds 27,728 characters while its body sits at #950 under the title *Planning Documents, Algorithms, and Diagnostics*, which holds 1,149,275. The monograph's own body_status reads `recovery=FULL-AT-DEPOSIT-950` — a pointer away from itself. Recovery was complete and nothing was lost; what did not survive was the shape of a book. The IDP is the interim correction, gathering pointers to what the archive holds and attachments for what it did not.

Eighteen workplan documents are attached, recovered from the generated-corpus-v1 release of the data-rhizome and hash-verified against the recovery index. Among them is `OS_NINE_VOLUME_SERIES_ARCHITECTURE.md`, which records the governing decision that *Operative Semiotics* ceases to be one book and becomes a nine-volume cycle — named not as an expansion but as a structural correction against a persistent compression strain in the single-volume build. The nine volumes take the names of the Muses: Calliope, Urania, Clio, Melpomene, Thalia, Polyhymnia, Terpsichore, Erato, Euterpe. Deposit #600, *The Muses as Operators*, is what makes that naming formal rather than ornamental.

Attribution within the package is deliberately three-way. The index is Cranes'; the book and its components are Johannes Sigil's; the workplans are Lee Sharks' as MANUS. An index does not absorb what it points at, and a package that flattened the three into a single creator would assert that the plan and the work were made by the same act.

lexical_attested_note: The package coins nothing. Its terms are drawn from the works it indexes — the nine-volume cycle and compression strain are the architecture document's, operative semiotics is Sigil's, the lacuna apparatus is EA-LACUNA-PROTOCOL-01's. An index that minted vocabulary would be making claims rather than locating them.

pairing_ruling.stated: semantic economy : operative semiotics :: political economy : praxis (operator, 2026-08-16)
pairing_ruling.what_it_settles:
OS is not a subdiscipline of the semantic economy, nor its application. The two are the paired halves of one structure, and the analogy fixes which half is which. Semantic economy is the ANALYTIC: how meaning is produced, circulated, extracted and liquidated under platform conditions. Operative semiotics is the PRAXIS: signs that intervene in the systems that read them.

The analogy also fixes the ORDER OF CONSTRUCTION. Praxis does not follow political economy as application follows theory — the critique of political economy is what produces the ground on which praxis becomes thinkable. Just so: the Marx reconstruction (Phase X) produces operative semiotics. That is why the reconstruction is UPSTREAM in this gather rather than adjacent to it.
pairing_ruling.what_it_forbids:
It forbids reading OS as 'everything the archive does operatively'. Praxis is not all action: activity without theory is mere activity, theory without action is contemplation, and praxis is the mode in which the two are ONE ACT. The corresponding test for OS is narrow and checkable:

  DOES THE DOCUMENT'S SEMIOTIC CLAIM DO THE THING IT DESCRIBES?

A room specification constitutes a room but advances no semiotic claim — not OS. A Notice of Semantic Strike withholds meaning while theorising the withholding of meaning — OS. An AXN specification inscribes what it theorises about inscription — OS. The test excludes most of the archive's 250-plus specifications and effective acts, which is what makes it a category rather than a mood.
pairing_ruling.consequence_for_venues: The journal structure already encodes the pairing and nobody planned it that way. TSEI takes the semantic economy — the analytic half. Grammata takes operative philology — philology that DOES something, which is the same predicate. A paper can be misfiled by being sorted to the analytic venue when it performs, or to the operative venue when it analyses, and the pairing gives a test for which.
pairing_ruling.consequence_for_the_gather: A seventh tier is warranted — PERFORMED: operative semiotics as praxis — for documents where the semiotic claim and the act coincide. It is NOT populated here, because populating it is a reading of ~250 specifications and effective acts against the test above, and that reading has not been done. Its absence is recorded rather than left to be inferred from a gather that stops at 34.
pairing_ruling.note_on_24: #24 Mind-Control Poems does name the discipline — twelve uses of 'operative semiotics', six of 'praxis', and the term is in its title. What it lacked was not the name but this framing. It is also, by content_type, an EFFECTIVE ACT: the only one of the archive's thirty-six that touches Marx or OS. So the first document of the performed tier is already in the gather, sitting in The Bridge, and its genre was the clue.

known_defect.what: This package points at #1343 as the Public Research Edition. #1343 carries the EXECUTIVE SUMMARY's body under that title. The Research Edition — the book — has no deposit. The package asserts an availability that does not exist and must be corrected once the text is located or the record retitled.
known_defect.also: Attachment links rendered as relative paths and 404'd from the record URL until 2026-08-16; fixed in wire_deposit.py.
